summary: The application exposes six exported components and requests eight dangerous permissions while code analysis detected 50 unsafe patterns across storage, network, crypto, and command execution, creating a high attack surface with several high‑to‑medium risk vulnerabilities.
top_risks: Runtime command execution via Runtime.exec (high risk)
Unvalidated WebView loadUrl enabling XSS or phishing (medium risk)
Hardcoded clear‑text HTTP endpoints exposing data to MITM (medium risk)
Insecure local storage (SharedPreferences/files) exposing credentials (low‑medium risk)
correlations: Exported activities may expose Runtime.exec methods without input validation
Dangerous permissions (e.g., ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, INTERNET) combine with hardcoded HTTP URLs to facilitate MITM attacks
Exported components linked to webview activity enable attackers to load malicious URLs
Publicly exposed SQLite activity allows SQL injection via intent data
SharedPreferences writes in exported activities risk credential leakage if not secured
vulnerability_candidates: Possibility of OS command injection using Runtime.exec on attacker‑controlled input
User‑supplied strings directly passed to rawQuery/execSQL resulting in SQL injection
WebView loadUrl invoked with unsanitized URLs can lead to XSS or phishing
Cleartext HTTP endpoints transmit authentication data unencrypted
Sensitive data stored in plain SharedPreferences or local files can be extracted after device compromise
recommended_next_steps: Sanitize and validate all inputs to Runtime.exec; restrict to safe utilities
Replace rawQuery/execSQL with prepared statements to prevent SQL injection
Validate URLs before WebView loadUrl; disable JavaScript when not needed
Migrate all HTTP endpoints to HTTPS and enforce via network security config
Encrypt sensitive data in SharedPreferences or use Keystore; enforce secure file permissions
